0.0.n: Refers to the item the speaker is showing or indicating.

0.1.n: Marks これ as the topic: what the speaker is talking about.

0.2.n: A noun naming a traditional Chinese pastry.

0.3.n: Politely finishes the statement identifying the item.

0.5.n: Repeated alone to emphasize the food’s name.

1.0.n: The Japanese food name is the topic being explained.

1.1.n: Marks 月餅 as the topic whose English name follows.

1.2.n: Names the language used to say the food’s name.

1.3.n: After a language name, で indicates which language is used.

1.4.n: The first part of ムーンケーキ, an English borrowing written in katakana.

1.5.n: Combines with ムーン to form the food name ムーンケーキ.

1.6.n: Politely completes the explanation of the English name.

1.8.n: The first part of ムーンケーキ, repeated to reinforce the English name.

1.9.n: The second part of the repeated food name ムーンケーキ.

1.10.n: Politely ends the repeated statement; the topic is left understood.

2.0.n: Names the language in which the food is called 月餅.

2.1.n: Marks 日本語 as the language used for the name.

2.2.n: Gives the Japanese name for the food already being discussed.

2.3.n: Politely completes the naming statement without repeating the topic.

2.5.n: The speaker repeats the Japanese name to help the listener remember it.

2.6.n: Adds a polite ending to the repeated food name.

3.0.n: Refers back to the mooncake being discussed.

3.1.n: Marks これ as the topic being described.

3.2.n: A conversational, emphatic version of とても that strengthens the following description.

3.3.n: 美味しい describes the taste; the attached です makes the statement polite.

3.5.n: Repeated with the description to emphasize how much the speaker enjoys the taste.

3.6.n: 美味しい stays unchanged before polite です; the topic is understood in this repetition.

0.lit: This, as for, mooncake is. Mooncake.
0.tip: これは…です is a polite pattern for identifying something: This is….

1.lit: Mooncake, as for, in English, moon-cake is. Moon-cake is.
1.tip: A language name followed by で tells you which language an expression is in.

2.lit: In Japanese, mooncake is. Mooncake is.
2.tip: Japanese often leaves out this or it when the topic is already clear.

3.lit: This, as for, very delicious is. Very delicious is.
3.tip: とっても is an emphatic, conversational alternative to とても, used before a description.
